name: Sync Shopify products and inventory levels to PostgreSQL

nodes.name: On Product Update
nodes.notes: Native Shopify webhook on products/update — fires on any product or variant change. Sample products are pinned so you can run the pipeline credential-free.

nodes.name: Map Product Header
nodes.notes: Maps the product-level fields for the products table.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO shopify_products (product_id, title, vendor, product_type, status, updated_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, NOW())
ON CONFLICT (product_id) DO UPDATE SET
  title = EXCLUDED.title, vendor = EXCLUDED.vendor,
  product_type = EXCLUDED.product_type, status = EXCLUDED.status, updated_at = NOW();

nodes.name: Upsert Product
nodes.notes: Upserts the product header keyed on product_id. Retries 3x; failure exits the error output.

nodes.name: Expand Variants
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: expands the product's variants array into one item per variant, carrying price and inventory quantity.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO shopify_variants (variant_id, product_id, sku, price, inventory_quantity, updated_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, NOW())
ON CONFLICT (variant_id) DO UPDATE SET
  sku = EXCLUDED.sku, price = EXCLUDED.price,
  inventory_quantity = EXCLUDED.inventory_quantity, updated_at = NOW();

nodes.name: Upsert Variant + Inventory
nodes.notes: Upserts each variant row (incl. inventory quantity) keyed on variant_id, so a stock change updates exactly one row. Retries 3x with backoff.

nodes.name: Capture Failure Context
nodes.notes: Error rail: captures which product/variant failed and why.

parameters.query: INSERT INTO shopify_dead_letter (order_id, error, payload, failed_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3::jsonb, NOW());

nodes.name: Write to Dead-Letter Table
nodes.notes: Error rail: parks the failed product/variant for later replay.

# Sync Shopify products and inventory levels to PostgreSQL for etl

**Pattern:** Data Sync & Integration · **Level:** Beginner · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers etl work end to end across Shopify and PostgreSQL.

It moves through 6 working steps plus a 1-node error rail, in this order:

1. On Product Update
2. Map Product Header
3. Upsert Product
4. Expand Variants
5. Upsert Variant + Inventory
6. Write to Dead-Letter Table

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing etl work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

On Product Update → Map Product Header → Upsert Product → Expand Variants → Upsert Variant + Inventory → Capture Failure Context → Write to Dead-Letter Table

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Shopify and PostgreSQL aligned by hand for etl
- Pushing etl events into Shopify and PostgreSQL the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Etl work where "Map Product Header" is still a manual step before Shopify
- Etl work that only reaches Shopify when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Shopify and PostgreSQL in step for etl, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Shopify or PostgreSQL call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 7 nodes in this etl build
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 7 nodes for etl before wiring Shopify
- 7 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for etl

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Shopify Admin API access token; Postgres connection.
Colour key: 🟦 entry · 🟫 app I/O · ⬜ logic · 🟩 output · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
This is event-driven; sample products are pinned so the pipeline runs with no credential. Sample data is pinned on the trigger, so hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow end to end before attaching a single credential. Right-click → Unpin when you go live.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never bundled in a template. Every node that talks to an external service needs its own connection before the first real run — open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Shopify Admin API access token**
Shopify Admin → Settings → Apps and sales channels → Develop apps → create an app → Admin API access token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant read_orders / read_products / read_customers as needed; the webhook trigger silently fails to register without the matching read scope.

**Postgres connection**
Host, port, database, user and password from your Postgres provider (Supabase, Neon, RDS, or self-hosted).
_Gotcha:_ Managed providers almost always require SSL — enable it in the credential options or the connection is refused.

Set each credential up once; it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens when the event should fire**
Cause: The workflow is still a draft, or its trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate it. The manual test URL is different from the production URL.

**A node shows a red triangle right after import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials note).

**Postgres node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL is off, or the n8n server IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed Postgres providers require both. Enable SSL in the credential options.

**Inventory quantity is always 0 or null**
Cause: products/update doesn't always carry live inventory levels for every setup.
Fix: For authoritative stock, subscribe to the inventory_levels webhook or call the Inventory API; this workflow reflects what the product payload reports.

**Variants aren't written**
Cause: The product has no variants array in the payload, or the Code node found none.
Fix: Every Shopify product has at least one (default) variant — check the pinned sample shape against your real payload.

Still stuck? The **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there.

## Design decisions

Products and variants are separate tables because inventory is a variant-level fact — collapsing them would make 'stock for SKU X' an awkward query. The product upsert runs before variants so a foreign key from variants -> products is always satisfiable. Both errors (product write and variant write) share one rail, so a failure anywhere in the product lands in one dead-letter table.

## Practice exercises

Already production-shaped — deepen it:

1. Add a low_stock boolean computed when inventory_quantity <= a threshold.
2. Delete variants in Postgres that no longer exist on the product (handle removals).
3. Also handle products/delete to soft-delete rows with a deleted_at timestamp.

## 🛠 Customize me

Product fields map in **Map Product Header**; variant and inventory fields in **Expand Variants**. Tables are `shopify_products` / `shopify_variants`. To handle removals, subscribe to `products/delete` and soft-delete rows. Add a `low_stock` computed column in the variants upsert.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Shopify: a custom app with only the order/product scopes read here.
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole etl payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.
